question: If $A$ and $B$ are invertible matrices of the same order, show that $B^{-1}A^{-1}$ is the inverse of $AB$.
explanation:
Right product
Using associativity of matrix multiplication, $$(AB)(B^{-1}A^{-1})=A(BB^{-1})A^{-1}=AIA^{-1}=AA^{-1}=I$$
Left product
$$(B^{-1}A^{-1})(AB)=B^{-1}(A^{-1}A)B=B^{-1}IB=B^{-1}B=I$$
Inverse of the product
Since multiplication in both orders gives $I$, $$\left(AB\right)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}$$

options.B: $B^{-1}A^{-1}$ is not an inverse of $AB$ because matrix multiplication is non-commutative.
